newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ governor to brief media on BOJ law revision.
newsitem.headline: BOJ governor to brief media on BOJ law revision.

text.p: Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita will hold a news conference at 5 p.m. (0800 GMT) following the passage in parliament's Upper House earlier on Wednesday of bills to revise the BOJ law, the BOJ said in a statement.
The revision of the decades-old BOJ law is aimed at freeing the central bank from the grip of the once-powerful Finance Ministry.

The BOJ law revision is part of the deregulation promoted by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, himself a former finance minister. Hashimoto hopes to reduce the authority of MOF, which has come under fire for its handling of Japan's banking crisis and various embarrassing scandals involving its senior officials.

The plan calls for a number of changes to give more freedom to the central bank in deciding the nation's monetary policy: -- The government can only ask the BOJ's policy-making board to postpone decisions on monetary policy, while at the present time it can order the central bank to do so.
-- Two government representatives who are currently members of the BOJ's policy-making board can attend meetings "only when necessary".
-- The finance minister would continue to approve the BOJ's budget, but only for costs other than those relating to money supply and monetary policy.

-- The minister would no longer have the authority to directly carry out an inspection of the BOJ. Any investigations on whether the BOJ had broken any laws or regulations would be made by BOJ auditors.
